newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.S. citizens donate medicine to Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.S. citizens donate medicine to Iraq.

text.p: Four U.S. citizens on Saturday said they had travelled to Baghdad to protest U.N. trade sanctions imposed on Iraq for invading Kuwait in 1990.
"We hope to fast for three days in front of the U.S. interests section at the Polish embassy," said Richard McDowell, a member of a Chicago-based group that has sent similar teams in the past.
"We are defying U.S. laws on sanctions. We do not believe they are just. We believe they are a crime against humanity," said McDowell, who is from Ohio.
McDowell said they donated $10,000 worth of medical supplies to Iraq's health ministry after the team from the Voices in the Wilderness group arrived on Thursday.
The four said their Baghdad visit was in defiance of a warning by the U.S. Treasury Department of stiff penalties and long prison terms if they went ahead with it.

"The U.S. government has told us in writing that if we come to Iraq we risk spending 12 years in prison and more than $1 million in fines. We sent them a letter and said: 'You do what you want'," McDowell said.
Since the 1991 Gulf War -- when a U.S. led force drive Iraqi troops out of Kuwait -- U.S. citizens have been barred from going to Iraq without special permission.
"We are using food and medicine as a weapon...What is America benefiting from all this suffering?" he said.
Iraq on Monday agreed to U.N. terms on a partial oil sale of $2 billion over six months to partly alleviate the suffering emanating from the U.N. embargo.
McDowell and the others said they were waiting for permission from Iraq to hold the hunger strike.
